summary: Build digital MEAL skills for indicator tracking, data quality, dashboards, and AI-assisted learning. Explore the practical course outline.
lede: Digital MEAL training shows programme teams how to turn field evidence into timely monitoring, evaluation and learning decisions. It is for MEAL practitioners and programme managers who need to track indicators, check data quality, visualize trends, and use community feedback to guide course corrections. Learners practise data review, dashboard planning, feedback-to-action workflows, and documenting adaptive decisions, with AI-assisted analysis subject to human validation.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who collect, analyse, govern, and use programme evidence across humanitarian, development, and public-sector settings. It suits beginners to intermediate practitioners with exposure to results frameworks, reporting cycles, or field monitoring.
prerequisites: You should have practical exposure to programme monitoring, results frameworks, field reporting, evaluation, or accountability processes. No coding or programming is required. Basic spreadsheet skills, including sorting, filtering, and simple formulas, will support the exercises. Bring a laptop with spreadsheet software if possible; supplied datasets and templates will support learners using different systems. Advanced AI and automation topics receive conceptual and operational treatment, while indicator tracking, data-quality review, dashboard specification, and adaptive planning receive hands-on practice.
